reports.title: BJ’s Wholesale Club Holdings, Inc. Announces Third Quarter Fiscal 2026 Results

desk.headline: Revenue up 17.5% to $6.28bn and EPS $1.73, both beat; full-year EPS guidance raised to $5.10–5.30

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted (equal to diluted GAAP this quarter)

results: Revenue rose 17.5% to $6.28bn, well above the $5.97bn estimate, helped a lot by gas sales; comparable sales excluding gas rose 4.1%.
EPS was $1.73 against $1.16 a year ago and a $1.24 estimate.
Profit was lifted by a roughly $240m gain from settling a card-fee lawsuit; about $95m of that was spent on members, staff and other investments.
Merchandise gross margin fell about 1.7 points because of heavy discounting during the 42nd birthday promotion.
Bought back $35.6m of shares in the quarter ($366.3m so far this year); two new clubs opened.

guidance.summary: BJ's raised its full-year outlook for comparable sales excluding gas and for adjusted EPS; capital spending stays about $800m.

points: The birthday promotion lifted traffic and units; management thought it added about a point to comparable sales but said that is a rough figure.
More than 200,000 new members joined in October; membership fee growth is expected to reach about 7.5% by year-end.
The lawsuit gain and some of the spending it funded will not repeat; margins outside the promotion were said to be on plan.
Management would not give a 2027 outlook and named diesel, medical and fuel costs as uncertainties.
Nearly 30 new clubs are planned for 2027–28, and the product range will be cut by about a fifth.
call.source: BJ's Wholesale Club Q3 Earnings Call Highlights — MarketBeat via Yahoo Finance, 20 Nov 2026
